This page updates from published facts. Starting a process alone never makes a step Ready.

  1. 4Start a workerStarting

    Waiting for a fresh heartbeat.

    Starting: Waiting for a fresh heartbeat.

    Starting a worker admits queued jobs and future matching events. Its preview names current manual jobs, armed schedules and reserve estimates. Stop or restart can interrupt work; it cannot undo spending.

    In a terminal instead
    pi-dispatch service install
    pi-dispatch worker

  2. 5Start the egress proxyNot yet

    Doctor on build3 reports a failing check. Every job is refused before it starts until the egress proxy runs.

    12 hosts in this deployment's allowlist. OpenShell uses gateway policy. Unsafe or shared proxy changes require the terminal.

    Review the allowlist
    In a terminal instead
    pi-dispatch up

  3. 6Provider keyNot yet

    Doctor on build3 reports a failing check. Use a configured API key or a bound, host-owned managed subscription. For API-key setup, set the key in the deployment's .env, then run doctor again.

    A configured API key or managed subscription is judged by doctor. An ordinary pi OAuth login is not unattended service authentication.

    Keep API keys for several providers. Add or replace a write-only key on Connections; the default provider stays unchanged.

    Manage provider API keys

    Official provider guides show where to find or create a key. Subscription sign-in uses its own host instructions.

    Review subscription authentication
    In a terminal instead
    pi-dispatch doctor

  4. 7Add a first triggerTo do

    A matching trigger starts a scheduled or forge job: a cron trigger for a folder, or a label, comment or pull request trigger for a repository. A manual run can be queued without a trigger.

    Fix issues labelled pi:fixA GitHub label runs flow fixTidy a folder every nightA local schedule runs flow tidyAnswer @pi in commentsA comment phrase runs flow fix

    Start from scratch in the trigger editor. Preview the exact added lines before saving.

    In a terminal instead

    In the operator panel, press a to add a trigger through the dialogs.

    /dispatch

  5. 8Forge credentialsOptional

    Only label, comment, issue and pull request triggers need them. Cron triggers on local folders run without.

    GitHub App creation and forge credentials stay in the terminal. Choose a webhook URL, or --no-webhook when using the poller.

    Review Connections
    Receiver service

    pi-dispatch service install --receiver
    In a terminal instead
    pi-dispatch setup github --webhook-url '<receiver URL>'

    Put the public URL of this deployment's pi-dispatch-receiver, where GitHub delivers events, in place of <receiver URL>; without a receiver, pass --no-webhook instead of --webhook-url and its URL.

  • Deployment foundThe console reads its files from the deployment in pi-dispatch.

  • Console tokenYou are signed in as an operator. Give people who only watch a viewer token.
Add a viewer

A one-use link, good for 60 seconds, grants a viewer session. The other person needs a route or their own tunnel to this console.

The one command

Use the durable installation from the Quickstart, then bootstrap the console on the deployment host.

pi-dispatch up --console

Or from pi, which opens this page for you:

/dispatch setup

Manage provider API keys, also after setup is ready.
